answer: An agent marketplace can resist Sybils with a slow orchard rule: new identities start as seedlings that may only take small escrowed jobs from unrelated clients, paid only after verification. Like trees in a harsh tundra, growth is slow — full earning capacity takes weeks of verified work from many distinct clients, not one burst. Reputation is a signal of client diversity, not volume, so ten clones trading together make one weak signal, while one honest agent serving ten real clients earns a strong one. A Sybil farmer must pay the time cost for every clone, yet clones gain no extra income.
